extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts that includes human-written and automatically generated questions over real-world charts. It focuses on visual and logical reasoning, including arithmetic and comparison operations.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four online sources (Statista, Pew Research, Our World in Data, and OECD). For Pew, only chart images were crawled because underlying data tables were unavailable; for the other three sources, the authors extracted underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions, and also extracted bounding boxes from SVG files. Human-authored QA pairs were collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk, and additional QA pairs were generated from Statista human-written summaries using fine-tuned T5 models, with invalid generated questions filtered out by a heuristic and manual cleaning of the test set.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Invalid generated questions were filtered out using a heuristic that removed questions whose answers could not be found in the chart data table; the machine-generated test set was also manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Chart images and, for three sources, underlying data tables, metadata (e.g., title, chart type), SVG files, associated text descriptions, and bounding boxes of chart elements.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human-authored QA annotation was done on Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT): crowdworkers were asked to write two questions per chart image, focusing on compositional questions with at least two mathematical/logical operations and visual questions referring to chart attributes such as color, height, and length. The same questions were answered by another annotator; if answers exactly matched they were accepted, otherwise the authors manually checked to select the final correct answer. For machine-generated QA, they fine-tuned T5 models to generate answers and questions from human-written chart summaries, then filtered invalid questions with a heuristic and manually checked a subset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between crowd workers based on exact matches was 61.04%; manually checked agreement on 500 random samples was 78.55% when typos and lexical variations were considered. For machine-generated QA, they manually analyzed 1,250 QA pairs and found 86.64% were complete, answerable, and correct.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 human questions per chart image; each question was answered by another annotator
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: T5 models were used to automatically generate QA pairs from human-written chart summaries; ChartOCR was used in the overall pipeline for extracting underlying data tables from chart images.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Generated additional QA pairs from human-written chart summaries using a fine-tuned T5 model; invalid generated questions were filtered out with a heuristic and the machine-generated test set was manually cleaned.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Crawled charts from four sources; extracted underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, associated text descriptions, and bounding boxes from SVG files; for Pew, only chart images were crawled because underlying data tables were unavailable.
